props.title: Class Action
props.initialSlug: Father-daughter lawyers clash in explosive lawsuit

sections.content: Class Action represents a pivotal legal drama that deftly explores the complex relationship between Gene Hackman's crusading civil rights attorney and Mary Elizabeth Mastrantonio's corporate defense lawyer - who happens to be his daughter. The film sits alongside other notable early 90s legal thrillers like The Firm (1993) and A Few Good Men (1992), but distinguishes itself by focusing on family dynamics within the justice system. Director Michael Apted, fresh off Gorillas in the Mist (1988), brings his documentary sensibilities to create an authentic courtroom atmosphere.

sections.content: The film's exploration of corporate malfeasance and whistleblowing connects it to later legal thrillers like Michael Clayton (2007) and Dark Waters (2019). What sets Class Action apart is its intimate focus on the ethical conflicts within a single family, using the father-daughter dynamic to personalize larger questions about justice and moral compromise. The automotive defect case at the center mirrors real-world cases like those depicted in Flash of Genius (2008) and Puncture (2011). SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Legal Drama

Class Action helped establish many conventions that would define legal thrillers of the 1990s and beyond. Its influence can be seen in films like Primal Fear (1996) and The Rainmaker (1997), where personal stakes intersect with broader social justice issues. The film's attention to procedural detail and focus on discovery and depositions created a template followed by The Insider (1999) and North Country (2005).
